project_name: Colusa Indian Energy / Strata Expanse AI and energy infrastructure campus
aliases: CIE Strata Expanse tribal lands AI campus
Colusa Indian Energy data center energy park
status_detail: Colusa Indian Energy announced a strategic partnership with Strata Expanse for an AI and energy infrastructure campus on tribal lands; reporting says the first facility uses surplus power from an existing 6 MW off-grid microgrid and later generation could total 100 MW as tenants are added.
notes: Included as a county super-set lead because Colusa Indian Energy is headquartered in Colusa and the Cachil Dehe Band's tribal land is in/near Colusa County, but the public article describes location as tribal land in Northern California rather than a county permit. Capacity listed as ultimate off-grid generation potential; initial microgrid surplus is 6 MW.

status_detail: City of Pittsburg project portal describes an approved AVAIO data center in the Pittsburg Technology Park; Phase I is a three-story 347,740 sq ft data center on about 22 acres of the former Delta View Golf Course, with supporting substation/switchyard and backup generation. City portal says the project received required City/state approvals; future phases need separate review.
notes: Official city pages give the strongest evidence. AVAIO states 99 MW secured capacity deployable in 2027 and up to 500 MW potential under the broader specific plan. Some local reporting cites 92-96 MW; retained 99 MW from developer/city-facing materials.

project_name: CalEthos Lithium Valley Data Center Campus
aliases: CalEthos clean-energy powered data center campus
status_detail: CalEthos announced an option to purchase 315 acres in Imperial County's Lithium Valley manufacturing zone for a first 100-acre/420 MW clean-energy powered data center campus, expanding from an earlier 80-acre/300 MW plan; DCD and company SEC exhibit describe Imperial County/IVEDC/IID coordination.
notes: Company/SEC release is primary evidence for 315 acres and 420 MW first phase; DCD confirms Imperial County Lithium Valley location. Later financial/market snippets suggest execution risk and possible abandoned prior site costs, so current status should be rechecked before investment-grade use.
